inspected.method: All 44 images actually viewed with view_image. Only RUBRIC.md and RUBRIC-r50.md read as text. Screenshots only; no interaction validation.

assessment_notes: Paired scores conservatively consider both sizes. Enlarged type and scrolling are accepted. Below-viewport content is not treated as inaccessible. The Standalone preview banner is ignored. No candidate meets the same-painted-hand threshold of 9.

ranking_notes: Combat is a visual tie across all four candidates within the instructed comparison scope; its serialized order uses system ranking as a neutral tie-break and is not evidence of a combat improvement.
winner_rationale: GARNET is the most coherent overall system across both sizes. Its restrained matte choice and record interiors avoid the stretched or inflated textures of the alternatives, and its shop provides the best painted velvet, natural card proportions and grounded carved support. Its named boundaries also distinguish the record's nested list. It still falls short of the references: flat footer strips, a synthetic memorial stage, crowded captions and unowned combat condition groups prevent a same-hand judgment.
winner_fixes: Gameover, center card stage: replace the black field of thin vertical gold lines with a painted cabinet or memorial alcove, with believable rear depth, contact shadows and a structural ledge.

Rest, event, gameover and shop, scrolling boundaries: replace the flat rectangular footer strips with painted structural rails or inset cartouches; keep the specific region names and put each cue in reserved space clear of text and controls.

Combat, upper condition groups: add owner nameplates and spatially group each condition set beside its owner; preserve clearance from actor silhouettes, shield crest, health/name bars and companion resource panel at both sizes.
Gameover, portrait shelf: separate the Maya and Bones subtitle areas so they do not visually run together at 1280x800; give each framed portrait its own caption width and line spacing.

Gameover, center progress cartouche: separate the progress count, wing designation and room name into a deliberate hierarchy so 'HOW FAR 2 WINGS EXPLORED' and the Nursery label do not read as one crowded sentence.

Rest, fort interior: paint a continuous rear wall and floor transition around the blankets so the vignette has believable depth instead of a dark cutout surround; retain the warm lantern pool and shelf.
Event, page and stand: unify the parchment edges, ornamental supports and room with shared candle highlights and contact shadows, keeping the existing readable introduction and choice strips.
Combat, upper-right How to play: replace the plain rounded rectangle with a gold-rimmed enamel or cartouche control matching the other utility controls.
Gameover, nested Final Tricks list: ensure the framed viewport ends at a deliberate boundary with no stray row fragments touching its footer; retain every item through scrolling.

grafts.idea: Use the double-rule cartouche treatment of its full-width Continue through story/choices/wares rails as the visual basis for GARNET's named boundaries, retaining GARNET's region-specific labels and separate cue placement.

Borrow the shop's quiet wood side jambs and deep dark velvet recesses where a simpler supporting structure is needed, while preserving GARNET's continuous carved shelf and natural embroidered curtain folds.

Borrow the event's visible stand feet and surrounding floor space to make the parchment support feel planted in the room; keep a clear reserved scroll boundary so the extra visible page does not end in an unexplained cut.
